hook.situation: You give a short presentation, answer a formal question, and then talk normally with a classmate afterward.
objectives: Use formal polite endings like -습니다, -ㅂ니다, and -습니까 in public or formal settings.
Choose between 해요체, 합쇼체, 존댓말, and 반말 based on relationship and setting.
Avoid using the stiffest style everywhere just because it feels safer.
hook.whyItMatters: Korean speech level is not decoration. The same idea can sound natural, stiff, friendly, distant, or rude depending on the ending and the relationship. A learner who says correct grammar in the wrong speech level can still sound socially off.

grammarNotes.title: V-(스)ㅂ니다 — the formal polite ending (합니다체)
grammarNotes.func: This is the formal polite ending for statements. It sounds more formal than the everyday -아요/-어요 (해요체) ending, so you hear it in announcements, at work, in the news, and when you first meet someone.

formTable.when: Stem ends in a vowel (no 받침)
formTable.ex: 가다 → 갑니다 / 오다 → 옵니다 / 크다 → 큽니다

formTable.when: Stem ends in a consonant (has 받침)
formTable.ex: 먹다 → 먹습니다 / 읽다 → 읽습니다 / 작다 → 작습니다

formTable.when: Stem ends in ㄹ (the ㄹ drops)
formTable.ex: 살다 → 삽니다 / 만들다 → 만듭니다 / 알다 → 압니다

examples.note: 이다 attaches to the noun 학생 as 입니다 — the standard way to introduce yourself.
먹다 has a 받침 (ㄱ), so it takes 습니다 → 먹습니다. 밥을 먹다 just means "to eat (a meal)".
가다 ends in a vowel, so it takes ㅂ니다 → 갑니다.
살다 ends in ㄹ, which drops before ㅂ; the question ending -ㅂ니까? makes it 삽니까?

keyPoint.label: 받침 decides ㅂ니다 vs 습니다
keyPoint.body: No 받침 → add ㅂ니다 (가 → 갑니다). Has 받침 → add 습니다 (먹 → 먹습니다). The one exception is ㄹ stems: the ㄹ drops and you use ㅂ니다 (살 → 삽니다), so they act like vowel stems.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: The ㅂ in -ㅂ니다 sounds like [m] before ㄴ: 갑니다 sounds like [감니다], 입니다 like [임니다], and 습니다 like [슴니다].

drill.instruction: Change each dictionary-form verb into the formal 합니다체 statement (V-(스)ㅂ니다).

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: The ending depends on the last letter of the stem, not the meaning. A stem ending in a consonant like 먹 takes 습니다 (not ㅂ니다), and a stem ending in a vowel like 가 takes ㅂ니다 (not 습니다). Check the stem's last letter first.

grammarNotes.title: Choosing the style — 해요체 vs 합니다체 vs 반말
grammarNotes.func: Korean changes the verb ending depending on who you're talking to. The three everyday styles are 해요체 (polite, all-purpose), 합니다체 (formal polite), and 반말 (casual, no -요). The listener and the situation pick the ending — not the meaning of the sentence — so the wrong choice can sound rude or oddly stiff.

formTable.when: 해요체 — polite, the default for daily life
formTable.ex: 가다 → 가요 / 먹다 → 먹어요 / 공부하다 → 공부해요

formTable.when: 합니다체 — formal polite (work, announcements, first meeting)
반말 — casual (close friends, younger people, family)
formTable.ex: 가요 → 가 / 먹어요 → 먹어 / 공부해요 → 공부해
all mean "(I) eat", from most formal to most casual

examples.note: 해요체 — the safe, friendly default for people you don't know well.
합니다체 — a formal first greeting; you'd hear this in business and formal settings.

examples.en: Hey, where are you going right now?
examples.note: 반말 — 가요 drops 요 to become 가; used with a close friend the same age. 너 (you) also marks 반말.
반말 — used at home with family; 배고파요 drops 요 to 배고파, and 나 (casual "I") fits the casual style.

keyPoint.label: The listener, not the meaning, picks the ending
keyPoint.body: 합니다체 = formal/distant (work, strangers, announcements). 해요체 = polite all-purpose (the safe everyday choice). 반말 = casual, only with close friends, younger people, or family. When unsure, use 해요체 — it's polite and never rude.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: In 반말 questions, the rising pitch alone marks the question: 가? rises at the end, while the statement 가. falls. There's no -까? ending and no spelling change.

drill.instruction: Rewrite each 해요체 sentence in the style named in brackets (합니다체 = formal, 반말 = casual).

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English has one neutral register, so learners drop 요 to sound casual and friendly — but 반말 can be disrespectful to someone older or senior. Default to 해요체 with anyone you aren't clearly close to, and switch to 반말 only once the relationship plainly allows it.

grammarNotes.title: 반말 4형 — casual statements, questions, commands, and let's
grammarNotes.func: 반말 is the casual style used with close friends, younger people, and some family members. For many everyday statements and questions, you can start from the 해요체 form and remove 요: 먹어요 → 먹어. Commands use the same -아/어 shape, while casual "let's" uses -자.

formTable.ex: 먹어요 → 먹어. / 먹어?; 가요 → 가. / 가?

examples.note: Statement: 가요 loses 요 → 가. 나 also matches the casual style.
Question: 먹었어요 loses 요 → 먹었어? The rising pitch makes it a question.
Command: 오다 becomes 와. This is only safe when 반말 is already okay.
Name + 아 calls someone with 받침; 가자 is the casual let's form.

keyPoint.label: 요-drop is grammar; permission is social
keyPoint.body: The form is simple: remove 요 for many statements and questions, use -자 for "let's," and use 야/이야 after nouns. The hard part is social timing. Switch to 반말 only after the relationship allows it, often after someone asks 말 놔도 돼요? or suggests 우리 말 놓을까요?

grammarNotes.pronunciation: In 반말 questions, spelling often stays the same as the statement and pitch does the work: 먹어. falls, 먹어? rises. With names, 지민아 flows as [지미나] because the final ㄴ links to 아.

drill.instruction: Change each polite sentence into natural 반말 for a close friend.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 반말 is just Korean slang, so it is okay with anyone if I sound friendly.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 반말 is a relationship signal. Use it only with close people, younger people, or when both sides have agreed.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: The form itself is not rude; the mismatch is rude. A perfect 먹어? can be warm to a close friend and very disrespectful to a teacher or stranger. Decide the relationship first, then choose the ending.

exampleSentence.ko: 친구가 아니면 처음에는 해요체로 말하는 게 안전해요.
exampleSentence.en: If they are not a friend, it is safe to speak in haeyo style at first.
In a presentation, formal polite style sounds natural.
I use casual speech with close friends.

exampleSentence.ko: 발표에서는 말투를 조금 더 격식 있게 바꿔야 해요.
exampleSentence.en: In a presentation, you need to make your tone a little more formal.
exampleSentence.note: Tone includes ending, word choice, and attitude.

exampleSentence.en: An interview is a formal setting.
I will begin the presentation now.
In an interview, I speak clearly in polite speech.
I use polite speech with the teacher.
With a close friend, casual speech sounds natural.
The way of speaking changes depending on the situation.
In a formal setting, I speak slowly.
exampleSentence.note: Verb that carries the speech level.

exampleSentence.en: I will begin the presentation now.

exampleSentence.note: Natural 해요체 after the public speech.

exampleSentence.en: It is okay to answer questions briefly.

readingText.title: One topic, two speech levels
readingText.body: 민서는 내일 수업에서 발표를 해요. 발표는 격식 있는 자리라서 처음에는 “지금부터 발표를 시작하겠습니다”라고 말할 거예요. 발표가 끝난 뒤에는 “질문 있으십니까?”라고 물을 수 있어요. 하지만 발표 후에 친구와 이야기할 때는 합쇼체를 계속 쓰지 않아요. 친구에게는 “발표 끝났어요”처럼 해요체가 더 자연스러워요. 친한 친구라면 반말도 가능하지만, 처음 만난 사람에게는 존댓말이 안전해요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo has a class presentation tomorrow. Since a presentation is a formal setting, she will begin by saying, 'I will begin the presentation now.' After the presentation, she can ask, 'Do you have any questions?' But when talking to a friend after the presentation, she does not keep using formal style. With a friend, haeyo style like 'The presentation is over' sounds more natural. Casual speech is possible with a close friend, but with someone you just met, polite speech is safe.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 발표 처음에 뭐라고 말할 거예요?

culturalNote.title: The most formal style is not always the most natural
culturalNote.body: Learners sometimes use 합쇼체 everywhere because it feels safest. Korean speakers may understand it, but with classmates or friendly staff it can sound stiff, distant, or scripted. Good Korean is not only polite; it fits the relationship.
culturalNote.tip: When unsure, start with 해요체. Move to 합쇼체 for formal public settings, and use 반말 only when the relationship allows it.

inlineExercises.prompt: For a formal presentation opening, choose:
inlineExercises.explanation: 합쇼체 fits a formal public opening.

inlineExercises.prompt: After the presentation, with a classmate, choose:
inlineExercises.explanation: 해요체 is natural for ordinary polite conversation.

inlineExercises.prompt: With someone you just met, the safe default is:
inlineExercises.explanation: Use polite speech first when the relationship is not close.

inlineExercises.prompt: Complete the formal statement: 저는 한국어를 공부___다.
Fix the sentence for a teacher: 선생님, 질문 있어?
inlineExercises.correct: 선생님, 질문 있어요? / 선생님, 질문해도 돼요?

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the over-formal classmate sentence: 발표를 종료하겠습니다.
inlineExercises.explanation: With a classmate after the formal setting, 해요체 sounds more natural.

inlineExercises.prompt: 선생님___ 질문이 있어요. (I have a question for the teacher.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 께 marks the respected recipient of the question. 께서 marks a respected subject doing an action, and 를 would wrongly mark the teacher as an object.
Formal polite statements use -ㅂ니다/습니다. 하다 verbs become 합니다, so 공부하다 becomes 공부합니다.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build a formal sentence: 'I study Korean.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 합니다체 is appropriate for presentations and interviews. 한국어를 stays as the object before the formal verb.

inlineExercises.prompt: After class, you speak casually with a close friend. Which ending fits best?
inlineExercises.explanation: With a close friend, 반말 can be natural. The other two are much more formal and would sound distant after class.

bullets: Use 합쇼체 for formal public settings: 발표를 시작하겠습니다.
Use 해요체 for ordinary polite conversation: 발표 끝났어요.
Use 반말 only when the relationship allows it.
존댓말 is the broad polite category; 해요체 and 합쇼체 are both polite styles.
Good Korean matches grammar, relationship, and setting together.

writingTask.prompt: Write the same short self-introduction twice — once for a job interview and once for a close friend — to show the difference in speech level.
writingTask.hint: Use the formal -(스)ㅂ니다 (합니다체) for the interview, and switch to 반말 (drop -요) for the friend.
writingTask.model: 면접에서는 이렇게 말합니다. "안녕하십니까? 저는 민수입니다. 잘 부탁드립니다." 친구한테는 이렇게 말해. "안녕? 나는 민수야. 잘 지내?"
writingTask.modelEn: In an interview I speak like this: "Hello. I am Minsu. I look forward to working with you." To a friend I say it like this: "Hi. I'm Minsu. How are you?"

canDo: Use the formal polite ending in formal settings (-(스)ㅂ니다, 합니다체)
Choose between 해요체, 합니다체, and 반말 to fit the listener
Switch into casual 반말 with a close friend (drop -요)
Match my speech level to the situation (발표 · 면접 · 친구)
